subject: Do Shiny apps work in remote locations? (With low internet bandwidth)

messages.author: 9fa4a098c0bc9af1
messages.subject: Do Shiny apps work in remote locations? (With low internet bandwidth)
parts:
Hello Shiny community,

I have been thinking about developing a Shiny app for one of my projects (I am an ecologist), in order to allow partners in different locations to visualize the data we collect together. I work with communities in remote locations where there is often limited internet access, and limited bandwidth. I was wondering if anyone has experience with this, and has suggestions on whether Shiny works in these circumstances or whether I should look for an alternative approach?

Thank you!

messages.author: c1629c4c1cffcc0e
messages.subject: Re: Do Shiny apps work in remote locations? (With low internet bandwidth)
parts:
Hey there Emma,

It seems to be okay in our experience, but a lot of it depends on how much data you will be sending to the client, as well as how much Javascript needs to be downloaded too.

One of our apps sent a large data frame to the client (using DT) and that was noticeable (1MB+). But not a deal breaker.

Prior to the recent versions with the better connection management, however, we did have a bit of a hard time accessing from, for example, a coffee shop. But now it seems significantly better. So make sure you are running the latest version and take advantage of the new connection enhancements.

Maybe others have a bit more insight on it than I do though!

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Do Shiny apps work in remote locations? (With low internet bandwidth)
parts:
+1 to what Laz said. I will tell you that the most recent version of Shiny Server added these config options (quoting from the NEWS file):

* Add additional configuration directives `http_keepalive_timeout`,
  `sockjs_heartbeat_delay`, and `sockjs_disconnect_delay` to allow working
  with very slow connections and large SockJS payloads. (The default values
  for these options are the same as in previous versions of Shiny Server.)

This was in response to customer reported problems where, if I recall correctly, users were on 2.5G cell phone connections trying to access renderDataTable output data that took a couple of minutes to transfer. Most sites won't have a need to change these values.
